edits.before: - Put `Clued-Work-Claim: <claim_id>` in the pull request body and as a trailer of the head commit, and add `Clued-Work-Scope: project:<id>` when the Task is not Global. The `clued-work-admission` check verifies the claim against the pull request's changed paths when it runs and, where the layer requires a claim, rejects a pull request whose claim is missing, expired, superseded or too narrow. Only that check binds the claim to the pull request: once the Owner has marked a CI admission Binding, a `clued_work_verify` call with `pr_ref` from any other Binding is refused (`admission_binding_required`), even after the marked Binding is revoked or expires, so call it without `pr_ref` to check a claim yourself. A passing check is not verified again at merge time; an hourly job turns it red once the claim no longer admits the pull request, so keep the claim live until the pull request merges. Each new pushed head counts toward the Task's CI meter (40 heads per Task in any 24 hours, all of its claims together); when the check reports `task_ci_head_cap_reached`, another claim does not help: push again after its `ci_retry_after`, or tell the Owner.
edits.after:
- Native is the single source of PR-to-Task identity: one PR has one Task, and a Task may have several PRs. Authorize each exact repository/head/target with the current holder key. A known PR number can be associated atomically with that authorization; otherwise qualified CI discovers it from one valid authorization of a current claim. Ambiguity, an obsolete key or generation, and an unauthorized head never fall back to body text, actor identity or a guessed scope. Claim/scope lines in bodies and commits are explanatory. Native resolves each PR to its Task and projects that Task's current claim, exact scope, fence and execution epoch. `resolve_pr_claim` is a projection, not `ADMITTED` or an execution grant, and does not consume the Task's CI-head budget. Ordinary and explicitly `read_only` observations cannot create or activate a relation. Only qualified CI, after observing the actual open PR and validating the current holder-key authorization for its exact repository/head/target, may activate it and emit the association Receipt. Unknown or closed relations retain their Task/scope for cleanup but provide no live execution claim and block no queue slot. Reclaim or handover follows the Task's new current claim; old keys and head authorizations stay obsolete. Normal renewal alone does not change that identity. Ordinary same-Task PRs do not terminate one another; the existing explicitly configured multi-copy winner/adoption rule remains in force.

- The `clued-work-admission` check then fully verifies that projected claim against the actual changed paths and exact PR target, including the role, scope, fence, epoch and holder-key authorization. Where the layer requires a claim, missing, expired, superseded, ambiguous or too-narrow authority refuses. An installed Source keeps its configured scope; an unspecified generic caller scope comes only from Native and never defaults to Global. Once the Owner has marked a CI admission Binding, a full `clued_work_verify` with `pr_ref` from any other Binding is refused (`admission_binding_required`), even after the marked Binding is revoked or expires. Use the read-only resolver to inspect an existing association and ordinary verification without `pr_ref` to inspect your claim. First discovery must remain possible through a normal holder-authorized push/create; it cannot require an already active PR relation. A passing check does not remove the later exact-head/current-generation merge checks or re-verification. Keep the claim live until merge. Each new pushed head counts toward the Task's CI meter (40 heads per Task in any 24 hours, all of its claims and PRs together); when the check reports `task_ci_head_cap_reached`, another claim does not help: push again after `ci_retry_after`, or tell the Owner.
